sana: Heads up — onboarding hit a weird failure when converting `hf/xyz-llama-chat-lite` to Redwood format. Conversion aborts with a mysterious attribute error and the chat template builder drops the system prompt.

sana: Root error snippet from our conversion run:
```
TypeError: 'CustomChatConfig' object has no attribute 'n_layers'
  File \"/app/convert.py\", line 412, in _from_config
    config.n_layers = config.model_layers
```

sana: The model's `config.json` contains `auto_map` that points at a repo with a custom class and also custom special tokens: "special_tokens_map": {"system_token": "<|sys|>", "pad_token": "<|pad|>"}. When the converter runs without remote code, our tokenizer output looks like:
```
Tokenizer: unk_token=<unk>, bos_token=None, eos_token=None, special_tokens_map={'system_token': '<|sys|>'}
ChatTemplateBuilder: system_prompt=""  # empty fallback
```

ken: This is the usual trust-remote-code scenario. The HF model relies on a custom config/class to expose expected attrs (n_layers, hidden_size mapping, etc). Two options: give the converter `trust_remote_code=True` or vendor a tiny shim that maps the names.

ken: Try: `rw-hf-convert --repo hf/xyz-llama-chat-lite --out redwood/xyz --trust-remote-code` or in Python: `AutoConfig.from_pretrained(repo, trust_remote_code=True)` and same for Tokenizer/Model.

oliver: If you can't enable remote code for security reasons, a minimal workaround is to patch the downloaded `config.json` before conversion. Example patch rules we used: map `model_layers` -> `n_layers`, `hidden` -> `hidden_size`, and remove `auto_map` entry so our loader doesn't try to instantiate remote classes.

oliver: Quick jq-ish transform we ran: 
```bash
curl -sL https://huggingface.co/hf/xyz-llama-chat-lite/raw/main/config.json \
  | jq '.n_layers = .model_layers | .hidden_size = .hidden | del(.auto_map)' > patched-config.json
```

eva: Note: when we allowed `trust_remote_code` in a sandbox we got past the attribute error but then hit a quantization mismatch during 4-bit tests — optimizer complained about missing state keys (q_proj vs query_proj) on load. Likely remote class uses different param naming.

sana: Right — the 4-bit quant run log: 
```
Loading state dict...
KeyError: 'model.encoder.layers.6.attention.q_proj.weight' not found. Available keys: ['qkv_proj.weight', 'attention.query.weight', ...]
```

oliver: That explains the evaluation regression too. With the remote class + trust_remote_code the model loads but our QAT/quant tooling remaps differently and tokens end up misaligned. Evals show generation quality drop ~8 ROUGE on our chat eval set after naive 4-bit quant.

ken: Two mitigation paths: 1) vendor a compatibility shim that inherits the remote class but renames parameters on load to our canonical names; 2) request the model author to add a `redwood_compat` entry in `config.json` listing param name aliases and special token canonical names.

sana: For immediate unblock I pushed a small shim into the conversion pipeline that does: after loading remote class, call `model = _apply_param_aliases(model, alias_map)` where alias_map is inferred heuristically (regex-based). It got the converter to finish and chat templates now pick up `system_prompt` correctly.

convert-bot: Model conversion succeeded for fork `redwood/xyz-llama-chat-lite` (sandbox). Output artifacts: converter-log.txt, patched-config.json, tokenizer.json, redwood-ready.tar.gz :party-parrot:

eva: Important ops note — if you run `trust_remote_code` we must run it in an isolated container image with pinned buildpack and no inbound network to the model repo. Ops will require a one-off security review.

ken: Agreed. For the public docs let's add a short checklist for HF models with `auto_map` or custom architectures:
- Check `config.json` for `auto_map` -> requires review
- Inspect `special_tokens_map` and canonicalize keys to Redwood names (`system`, `user`, `assistant`)
- Try conversion with `trust_remote_code=True` in sandbox; compare state dict keys
- If using quantization, run param-name aliasing step then run quant evals

sana: I'll open a PR with the shim + a test case (small toy model with mismatched names) and a short runbook for SEs. Also adding an eval job to fail the onboarding if chat template ends up with empty system prompt.

oliver: Thanks — that runbook will save time. Also let's add a short CLI flag `--map-special-tokens` to the converter so we can auto-rename `<|sys|>` -> `<|system|>` etc.

sana: Will do. If anyone wants to repro locally, steps in thread + I'll link the sandbox fork once CI finishes. :eyes:

ken: Nice catch — this was subtle. :thinking:

oliver: Good job catching the empty system prompt; those regressions are sneaky. :thumbsup:
